title: Semantic version ranges
prompt: Implement `satisfies(version, range, options = {})` and `maxSatisfying(versions, range, options = {})` in `src/range.js` (stubs that throw): semantic-version ranges in the style of npm. Versions. A version is exactly `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, then optionally `-` and a prerelease, then optionally `+` and build metadata. Major, minor and patch are decimal numbers with no leading zero (`0` is fine) that are safe integers. A prerelease is dot-separated identifiers, each either a number with no leading zero or a string of letters, digits and hyphens containing at least one letter or hyphen (`0a`, `a-b`, `7` are fine, `01` and an empty identifier are not). Build metadata is dot-separated non-empty identifiers of letters, digits and hyphens and is ignored everywhere. No leading `v`, no spaces. A string that is not a version throws `Error('invalid version: <text>')`; a version that is not a string throws `TypeError('version must be a string')`. Precedence is as in semver 2.0: compare major, minor and patch as numbers; a version with a prerelease is lower than the same without; two prereleases are compared identifier by identifier, numbers by value, strings by ordinary character order (so `Alpha` is lower than `alpha`), a number is lower than a string, and when all the shared identifiers are equal the one with fewer identifiers is lower. Ranges. A range is comparator sets separated by `||` (spaces around it are allowed); a version satisfies the range if it satisfies any set. An empty set (an empty or blank range, `||`, or `1.2.3 ||`) matches every version. A set is either one hyphen range, `A - B` (spaces around the `-`), or comparators separated by spaces, which must all hold. A comparator is an optional operator, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `=`, `~` or `^`, immediately followed (no space) by a partial version: one to three of major, minor and patch, where a missing part, or a part written `x`, `X` or `*`, is a wildcard (and a wildcard makes everything after it a wildcard), optionally followed by `-prerelease` only when all three numbers are given (build metadata is ignored). `*` alone, or no partial at all, matches everything. Anything else throws `Error('invalid range: <range>')` with the whole range as given (a range that is not a string too, written as a string). What each form means. A partial with no operator or `=` is the family it names: `1` is >=1.0.0 and <2.0.0, `1.2` and `1.2.x` are >=1.2.0 and <1.3.0, and a full version means exactly that version. With an operator a partial means the family: `>1.2` is >=1.3.0, `>=1.2` is >=1.2.0, `<1.2` is <1.2.0, `<=1.2` is <1.3.0, `>1` is >=2.0.0, `<=1` is <2.0.0; `>*` and `<*` match nothing, `>=*` and `<=*` match everything. Tilde: `~1.2.3` is >=1.2.3 and <1.3.0, `~1.2` is >=1.2.0 and <1.3.0, `~1` is >=1.0.0 and <2.0.0. Caret keeps the leftmost non-zero part fixed: `^1.2.3` is >=1.2.3 and <2.0.0, `^0.2.3` is >=0.2.3 and <0.3.0, `^0.0.3` is >=0.0.3 and <0.0.4; with a partial, `^1.2` and `^1.2.x` are >=1.2.0 and <2.0.0, `^0.2` is >=0.2.0 and <0.3.0, `^0.0` and `^0.0.x` are >=0.0.0 and <0.1.0, `^1` and `^1.x` are >=1.0.0 and <2.0.0, and `^0` and `^0.x` are >=0.0.0 and <1.0.0. Hyphen: `1.2.3 - 2.3.4` is >=1.2.3 and <=2.3.4; a partial lower end is padded with zeros (`1.2 - 2.3.4` is >=1.2.0); a partial upper end means the family (`1.2.3 - 2.3` is <2.4.0, `1.2.3 - 2` is <3.0.0); a wildcard end has no bound on that side. A prerelease in a full version is kept on the bound it makes (`^1.2.3-beta.2` is >=1.2.3-beta.2 and <2.0.0). Prereleases. A version that has a prerelease satisfies a set only if, as well as holding for every comparator in it, at least one comparator in that same set names a version with a prerelease and the same major, minor and patch. So `1.2.3-beta.2` satisfies `>=1.2.3-beta.1` and `^1.2.3-beta.1`, but `1.2.4-beta.1` does not satisfy `>=1.2.3-beta.1 <2.0.0`, `1.0.0-alpha` does not satisfy `*`, and `2.0.0-rc.1` does not satisfy `<2.0.0` (although it is lower) but does satisfy `<2.0.0-rc.2`. With `options.includePrerelease` exactly `true` that extra condition is dropped and a version is judged by precedence alone. `maxSatisfying(versions, range, options)` returns the highest version in the array that satisfies the range, as the string that was in the array; of versions that are equal in precedence (they differ only in build metadata) it returns the first; entries that are not valid versions are skipped; it returns `null` when none satisfies. A bad range throws as above. Run `npm test` to check your work.

origin.note: Second tranche. Caret, tilde, x-ranges, hyphen ranges, operators on partial versions, the prerelease rule and the precedence order, each stated exactly.
